strengths: Well-motivated problem: inducing elasticity directly in the factorized weight space for 'train-once, deploy-everywhere' deployment is a useful and timely direction, and the paper is, to my knowledge, among the first to formalize nested submodel training in the low-rank regime.

The theoretical section is a genuine contribution: Theorems 4.1–4.3 cleanly characterize why post-training selection (PTS) and all-subspace learning (ASL) fail and why nested submodel learning (NSL) recovers the Pareto front in the linear setting, with full proofs in App. B (measure-theoretic nongenericity argument, spectral interference analysis, induction on nested minimizers). These results give real insight and inform the method design.

Broad experimental coverage across architectures and scales: GPT-2, Llama-3.2-1B/3B and Llama-3.1-8B, and DINOv3 ViTs from ViT-L/16 up to ViT-7B/16, with comparisons to SVD/DataSVD, DRONE, SVD-LLM, ACIP (the SOTA elastic low-rank method), LLM-Pruner, and LayerSkip, plus a matched-budget independent-submodels baseline that isolates the benefit of weight sharing.

The ablations are thorough and well-designed: ranking-preservation of the DP probe is validated on an exhaustively searchable 10^4-submodel setting (Spearman 0.991, 94.1% exact match, low regret); Fig. 7(b) convincingly shows independent layer training fails while end-to-end consolidation works; Fig. 8 confirms the need for joint submodel training.

GAR (gauge-aligned reparametrization) is a practical contribution that avoids the dense r×r block, and the authors apply it uniformly to baselines (Remark 5.1), which is a fair-comparison practice; App. D.4 includes empirical runtime measurements supporting the theoretical cost model.
The limitations discussion (training memory/compute overhead ~2x, no adaptive routing evaluation, dependence on training data quality) is honest and specific rather than perfunctory.
weaknesses: There is a substantial gap between the theory and the method as applied. The Theorems 4.1–4.3 concern a single linear matrix with Frobenius reconstruction loss, while the actual method operates on deep nonlinear networks with distillation loss. The key bridging assumptions (ranking preservation under an additive error probe, preservation of relative submodel optimality through training, Sec. 3.2) are empirically validated only in a tiny MNIST/CNN-MLP setting (App. C.3, D.1); no evidence is provided for these assumptions on the actual Llama/ViT experiments where the claims matter most.

Main results (Fig. 4, Fig. 5) appear to be single runs without seed variance or confidence intervals, in contrast to Table 1 which reports standard deviations. Given the modest margins over some baselines in Fig. 5 and the sensitivity of LLM zero-shot evaluations, this weakens the evidential support for 'most graceful degradation'.

Comparison fairness concerns: the matched-budget protocol is argued but each competitor is trained/tuned under a different regime; the strongest elastic baselines (FlexTron, LlamaFlex) are not compared at all (justified by missing code/proprietary data), and the concurrent rank-elasticity work of Rauba & van der Schaar (2026) is discussed but not compared. The independent-submodels baseline appears only for Llama-3.2-1B.

Deployment claims are not fully substantiated: the abstract and introduction promise 'practical inference savings' and deployment relevance, but wall-clock measurements (App. D.4, Fig. 10) cover a single matrix shape (m=n=4096) on one GPU; no end-to-end latency/throughput for actual Llama/ViT models is reported, and the GAR reparametrization with a leading identity block may interact unfavorably with real transformer kernels.

Post-adaptation results (Table 1) show significant degradation at reduced budgets (e.g., code accuracy drops from ~18-37 to ~1-7 at 0.4x), suggesting the graceful-degradation property is much weaker after downstream finetuning; the paper does not discuss this tension.

Several correctness/editorial defects: Corollary B.8 states the suboptimal solution satisfies (Û,V̂) ∈ M/:= {...}, where the proof intends non-membership (also the corollary statement contradicts its own proof sketch); App. C.1 contains a circular definition (Δθl = (Δθl − UlVl⊤)); the footnote 'Code available at' is empty, harming reproducibility despite otherwise detailed experimental appendices.

The impact of the DP nestedness constraint on solution quality is not ablated (nested chain is enforced post-hoc in Algorithm 2's NESTEDCHAIN step); the cost of dropping Pareto-optimal but non-nested configurations is not quantified on real models.
